key_insight: Human and LLM-generated synthesis recipes perform comparably, and their closed-loop collaboration can accelerate discovery of new materials, including a new Ba3PtO5 structure.
engineering_relevance: This workflow shows how human-AI co-design can improve synthesis planning for complex materials spaces where prediction alone is not enough to deliver experimentally realizable discoveries.
method: Selected the Ruddlesden-Popper homologous series as a testbed spanning known and likely undiscovered materials.
Had humans and LLMs generate synthesis recipes for known and unknown candidates.
Validated recipes experimentally and fed results back into a closed-loop collaboration cycle.
evidence_signal: Experimental success rates were reported for humans vs. LLMs across two rounds, with similar performance on known materials and lower but measurable success on unknown targets, culminating in discovery of Ba3PtO5.
watch_item: Results may depend strongly on the chosen materials family and experimental execution, so performance may not transfer directly to other chemistries without retraining or expert oversight.
paper_title: Human and LLM Collaboration for Accelerated Materials Synthesis and Discovery
